content.title: About
content.content: Gluten‑free crackers are crisp snack biscuits made from gluten‑free grains such as rice, corn or buckwheat and flavored with a variety of seasonings like cheese, herbs or spices. They are suitable for people with celiac disease and anyone following a gluten‑free diet.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gluten‑free crackers are often used as a base for canapés and bite‑size appetizers.
Flavorings can be natural (herbs, spices) or artificial, but are always listed on the label.
Compared with whole‑grain crackers, gluten‑free versions may have lower fiber content, so they are frequently fortified with vitamins and minerals.
In many countries gluten‑free products must carry the “gluten‑free” label according to international standards.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Gluten‑free grains like rice and corn are easier to digest for those sensitive to gluten, reducing the risk of intestinal irritation.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Most gluten‑free crackers are baked with little added fat, making them suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Fortified varieties may contain thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Some recipes include added iron, calcium or magnesium, beneficial for bones and muscles.

items.title: Hypoallergenic
items.content: The absence of gluten makes these crackers safe for individuals with celiac disease or gluten intolerance.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Crackers may contain soy sauce, dairy flavorings or nuts, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Flavored versions often contain added salt; people monitoring sodium should choose low‑salt options.

items.title: Reduced fiber
items.content: Compared with whole‑grain products, gluten‑free crackers can have less dietary fiber, affecting satiety.

items.title: Potential additives
items.content: Some flavorings may be artificial; if preferred, select products labeled with “natural flavor.”

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Gluten‑free crackers can be enjoyed as a snack on their own, paired with cheese, hummus, pâtés, or used as a base for mini‑sandwiches. Lightly warming them in the oven can enhance their crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. Once opened, consume within 2–3 weeks to maintain crispness.
